sentence: This project builds imaging tools that find and treat colorectal adenomas without sedation, as a less invasive way to screen for colorectal cancer.
This project studies how myopia affects three types of retinal cells and how that relates to glaucoma, using a non-human primate model of myopia.
This project uses synthetic biology to change how cells decide their fate, aiming at the gradual cell decline seen in cancers, diabetes and neurodegenerative diseases.
This project studies how the quality of cancer care differs between Medicare Advantage and Traditional Medicare, and how limited provider networks affect that care.
This project studies how the frontal part of the brain, thalamus and cerebellum relate to attention deficit, and looks for genetic factors behind it.
This project studies how a mutation found in childhood brain cancer changes the DNA damage response, the tumor immune environment and treatment response.
This project makes zebrafish models of patient sequence variants, so their effects on human disease can be studied.
This project studies how nerve cells and immune cells communicate during chemotherapy-induced nerve pain, and whether boosting pain-relieving immune cells could help.
This project combines biological research with data science to study complex datasets about biological systems and human diseases.
This project develops software that sharpens magnetic resonance brain images and corrects their tissue contrast, so brain images can be measured automatically.
This project builds methods for studying how social and behavioral factors affect cancer risk, screening, treatment and prevention.
This project studies how calcium deposits form under the retinal pigment epithelium in macular degeneration and Alzheimer's disease, using cell models and human eye tissue.
This project studies how epithelial stem cells decide their fate, including how stem cells compete for space and how pH changes affect those decisions.
This project helps behavioral scientists understand, prevent and treat health disorders by adding biological and biomedical foundations to their work.
This project studies a muscle disorder that causes attacks of weakness, and tests drug and gene therapy approaches to prevent attacks and later weakness.
This project studies how La Crosse virus interacts with a host factor called JAG2 to enter cells, and what those interactions do to infection.
This project uses polygenic risk models and mammographic AI to predict risk of fast or slow growing breast cancer and tailor screening to it.
This project studies how extracellular polysaccharides are made and placed on the cell surface of Gram-negative bacteria.
This project studies how the way the cell nucleus organizes its genome controls fibroblast activation, a central driver of fibrosis.
This project studies the structure of potassium channels that respond to a cell's energy state, to understand their activity and design better drugs.
